triples.source_text: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar. He said, “Strike the atonement cover, and the foregates will shake; cut through the heads of all. I will kill their survivors with a sword. No one fleeing from among them will escape, and no one seeking safety will be saved.

target_units.text: and flight will perish from the runner, the mighty one will certainly not maintain his strength, and the fighter will certainly not save his life,
and the archer will certainly not stand, the swift of foot will certainly not be saved, nor will the horseman save his life,

triples.relationship: same-book warning that flight and strength cannot save
triples.rationale: Amos 9 says no fleeing person will escape and no one seeking safety will be saved. Chapter 2 likewise denies safety to the runner, fighter, archer and horseman. The later vision renews the book's warning that attempted escape and military ability will fail.

triples.source_text: If they burrow into Hades, My hand will pull them up from there; if they climb to heaven, I will bring them down from there.

target_units.text: Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.

triples.relationship: heaven and Hades cannot place a person beyond God's reach
triples.rationale: Amos names Hades and heaven as extremes from which the Lord will still retrieve fugitives. The psalm likewise asks where one can flee God's presence, then names heaven and Hades and describes His hand's reach. Amos applies the shared spatial contrast to judgment.

triples.source_text: If they hide on Carmel’s summit, I will search them out and take them from there. If they plunge from My eyes into the sea’s depths, I will command the dragon there, and it will bite them.

target_units.text: If a person hides in hidden places, will I not see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord.

triples.relationship: hidden places cannot conceal people from the Lord
triples.rationale: Amos describes the Lord searching out people hidden on Carmel and reaching those in the sea's depths. Jeremiah likewise asks whether a person hiding in hidden places can remain unseen by the God who fills heaven and earth.

triples.source_text: If they go into captivity before their enemies, I will command the sword there, and it will kill them. I will fix My eyes upon them for evils and not for good things.”

target_units.text: Because I have fixed My face upon this city for evils and not for good things. It will be handed into Babylon’s king’s hands, and he will burn it down with fire.

triples.relationship: parallel expression of divine attention for evils rather than good
triples.rationale: Amos announces eyes fixed upon the people for evils and not for good things. Jeremiah uses the corresponding expression of the Lord's face fixed upon the city for evils and not for good things. The connection is that stated direction of judgment, while the surrounding accounts treat captivity differently.

triples.source_text: The Lord, Lord God Almighty, touches the earth and shakes it; all who dwell in it will mourn. Its consummation will rise like a river and descend like Egypt’s river.

target_units.text: Will the earth not be disturbed over these things, and everyone dwelling in it mourn? A consummation will rise like a river and descend like Egypt’s river.

triples.relationship: same-book recurrence of earth's disturbance and Egypt's river
triples.rationale: Both passages join disturbance of the earth with its inhabitants mourning and a consummation rising like a river and descending like Egypt's river. Amos 9 explicitly introduces the Lord's touch as the earth is shaken.

triples.source_text: He builds His ascent into heaven and establishes His promise upon the earth; He calls for the sea’s water and pours it upon the earth’s surface. The Lord God Almighty is His name.

target_units.text: making all things and refashioning them, turning death’s shadow into morning and darkening day into night; He calls for the sea’s water and pours it upon the earth’s surface. The Lord God Almighty is His name,

triples.relationship: same-book repeated description of the Lord's power over waters
triples.rationale: Both passages describe the Lord calling for the sea's water and pouring it upon the earth's surface, followed by the declaration that the Lord God Almighty is His name.

triples.source_text: “Are you not like the children of Ethiopians to Me, children of Israel?” says the Lord. “Did I not bring Israel up from Egypt’s land, the foreigners from Cappadocia and the Syrians from a pit?

target_units.text: “I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

triples.relationship: explicit recollection of Israel's departure from Egypt
triples.rationale: Amos includes bringing Israel up from Egypt among the Lord's recalled acts. Exodus identifies the Lord as the One who brought the people out of Egypt and the house of bondage.

triples.source_text: “Are you not like the children of Ethiopians to Me, children of Israel?” says the Lord. “Did I not bring Israel up from Egypt’s land, the foreigners from Cappadocia and the Syrians from a pit?

target_units.text: And the Hivites who dwelt in settlements as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians who came forth from Cappadocia blotted them out, and dwelt in their stead.

triples.relationship: parallel recollection of migration from Cappadocia
triples.rationale: Amos recalls the foreigners being brought from Cappadocia. Deuteronomy describes Cappadocians coming from Cappadocia and settling in the place of the Hivites as far as Gaza. The connection is the stated movement from Cappadocia, without substituting another geographical name.

triples.source_text: Look, the Lord God’s eyes are upon the kingdom of sinners, and I will remove it from the earth’s surface. Yet I will not completely remove Jacob’s house,” says the Lord.

target_units.text: and they will devour your harvest and your bread, and devour your sons and daughters, and devour your sheep and calves, and devour your vineyards and fig orchards and olive groves; and with a sword they will thresh your fortified cities, in which you have trusted.
And it will be in those days, says the Lord your God: I will certainly not bring you to a complete end.

triples.relationship: announced devastation qualified by preservation from a complete end
triples.rationale: Amos announces removal of the kingdom of sinners but explicitly limits it by saying Jacob's house will not be completely removed. Jeremiah likewise announces an invading nation's destruction of produce and fortified cities, then promises not to bring the people to a complete end.

triples.source_text: “For look, I am giving a command: I will winnow Israel’s house among all the nations as one winnows in a winnowing basket, and no fragment will fall to the ground.

target_units.text: Simon, Simon, behold, Satan demanded to have you all, to sift you like wheat.

triples.relationship: winnowing and sifting applied to people
triples.rationale: Amos pictures Israel's house among the nations as being winnowed in a basket. Luke describes Satan's demand to sift Simon and those addressed with him like wheat. Both apply agricultural separation imagery to people, with different agents and settings.

triples.source_text: All the sinners of My people will die by a sword, those who say, ‘Evils certainly will not draw near or come upon us.’

target_units.text: Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.

triples.relationship: judgment against sinful people who deny approaching calamity
triples.rationale: Amos condemns sinners who insist that evils will not come upon them. Micah likewise presents corrupt leaders claiming that calamities will not come, then announces Zion's devastation because of them.

triples.source_text: On that day I will raise David’s fallen tent; I will rebuild its fallen parts, raise its demolished parts and rebuild it as in days of old,

target_units.text: With this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written:
‘After these things I will return and rebuild David’s fallen tent. I will rebuild its ruins and set it upright,

triples.relationship: explicit later use of David's fallen-tent promise
triples.rationale: Amos promises to raise and rebuild David's fallen tent and demolished parts. Acts introduces a prophetic quotation about rebuilding David's fallen tent and ruins, directly corresponding to that promise.

triples.source_text: so that the remaining human beings and all the nations over whom My name is called may seek,” says the Lord God, who does these things.

target_units.text: so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things
known from long ago.’

triples.relationship: explicit later use of the nations-seeking promise
triples.rationale: Amos speaks of remaining human beings and nations over whom God's name is called seeking. Acts' prophetic quotation likewise names the rest of humanity seeking the Lord and nations upon whom His name has been called. Amos's remaining-human-beings wording is preserved.

triples.source_text: “Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when threshing will overtake the vintage and grapes will darken to ripeness at seedtime. The mountains will drip sweetness, and all the hills will be planted together.

target_units.text: On that day mountains will drip sweetness, hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s water outlets will flow with water. A spring will come out of the Lord’s house and water the Wadi of Rushes.

triples.relationship: shared promise of mountains dripping sweetness
triples.rationale: Amos pictures renewed agricultural abundance with mountains dripping sweetness. Joel uses the same mountains-dripping-sweetness image alongside hills flowing with milk and abundant water.

triples.source_text: I will reverse the captivity of My people Israel. They will build ruined cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, plant gardens and eat their fruit.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: On the day I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the wilderness places will be rebuilt.
The devastated land will be worked, instead of lying devastated before every passerby’s eyes.
They will say, “That devastated land has become like a garden of delight, and the deserted, devastated, razed cities stand fortified.”
The nations remaining around you will know that I, the Lord, have rebuilt the razed places and planted the devastated places. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.

triples.relationship: parallel restoration of cities and cultivated land
triples.rationale: Amos promises ruined cities rebuilt and inhabited, with vineyards and gardens yielding food and drink. Ezekiel likewise promises inhabited rebuilt cities and cultivated devastated land, comparing it with a garden of delight.

triples.source_text: I will plant them upon their land, and they will certainly never again be uprooted from the land I have given them,” says the Lord God Almighty.

target_units.text: I will establish an eternal covenant with them, which I will certainly not turn back from behind them. I will put My fear in their heart so that they do not depart from Me.
I will attend to them to do them good and will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all heart and all soul.

triples.relationship: lasting settlement pictured as the Lord planting His people
triples.rationale: Amos promises that the Lord will plant the people in their given land without future uprooting. Jeremiah announces an eternal covenant and promises to plant the people in the land in faithfulness, likewise depicting their settlement as the Lord's planting.

I will kill their survivors with a sword. No one fleeing from among them will escape, and no one seeking safety will be saved.

target_units.text: In the year that King Oziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up; and the house was full of His glory.
And seraphim stood around Him: each one had six wings, and each one had six wings; with two they covered their faces, and with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
And one cried to another, saying: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Sabaoth; all the earth is full of His glory.
And the lintel was lifted at the sound of their cry, and the house was filled with smoke.

unresolved_candidates.reason: Both passages describe seeing the Lord in a sacred setting, but Amos commands a blow to the atonement cover with foregates shaking, while Isaiah describes a lintel lifted at the seraphim's cry. A sufficiently particular additional relationship was not retained from the general vision resemblance.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: “For look, I am giving a command: I will winnow Israel’s house among all the nations as one winnows in a winnowing basket, and no fragment will fall to the ground.

target_units.text: And I will scatter them in a dispersion; at My people’s gates they were bereaved; they destroyed My people because of their evils.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The proposed winnowing parallel does not occur in this supplied Jeremiah wording, which speaks of scattering in a dispersion and bereavement. No basket or winnowing image was imported into that text; this proposed image correspondence is unretained.
